authoring.author_context: fresh subagent context in an isolated worktree based on aae2a07

coordinator_adjudication.summary: Three of the seven findings rested on an instruction the coordinator had written too broadly in the author prompt, namely that no plan may deliberately force a deallocation error. On rereading the source the coordinator narrowed that rule rather than letting correct plans be deleted.
coordinator_adjudication.narrowed_rule: A plan may exercise an error condition that the standard specifies deterministically, provided its oracle asserts only portable properties. It must not depend on resource exhaustion, on a specific processor-dependent error value, or on manufacturing a stopped or failed image.
source_basis: 9.7.3.2 p1: deallocating an unallocated allocatable variable causes an error condition; its only prohibitions concern argument and construct association, so such a program with STAT= is conforming.
9.7.3.3 p1: the corresponding deterministic error conditions for pointer targets.
9.7.4 p5: the stat-variable becomes a processor-dependent positive value distinct from STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE and STAT_FAILED_IMAGE.
9.7.4 p6: the per-object status guarantees after an error condition.
9.7.3.1 p3: without a STAT= specifier an error condition causes error termination, so that facet cannot be an ordinary passing run.
coordinator_adjudication.reviewer_response: The reviewer explicitly accepted the adjudication with its own anchors and confirmed it does not read these STAT= forms as non-conforming or the positive-and-distinct assertion as unportable.

findings.defect: The catalogue title said 'DEALLOCATE statement'; the actual title is 'Form of the DEALLOCATE statement'.
findings.correction: Title corrected in the catalogue and generated view.

findings.defect: A plan proposed a no-STAT deallocation error.
findings.correction: Retained as a source-only plan that records that 9.7.3.1 p3 requires error termination, so it cannot be an ordinary passing run and would need an error-termination harness.

findings.defect: A plan deallocated a known-unallocated allocatable with STAT=.
findings.correction: Retained; the oracle now asserts only that the stat-variable is positive and distinct from both named constants, plus the 9.7.4 p6 retained status, and records that this is a deterministic standard-specified error rather than a resource failure.

findings.defect: Plans deallocated a disassociated pointer and a target not created by ALLOCATE.
findings.correction: Retained with the same portable oracle bounds; no target is dereferenced after the failed deallocation.

findings.defect: A plan proposed producing a stopped or failed image to observe STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE or STAT_FAILED_IMAGE.
findings.correction: The facet is now source-only and gated, and explicitly forbids manufacturing, forcing or relying on creating that condition.

findings.defect: The packet covered only direct coarray deallocation, omitting the source's second trigger: an allocate-object that has a coarray potential subobject component.
findings.correction: One new pending facet, S9.7.3.2-012.coarray-potential-subobject-component-trigger, covers the second trigger and is distinct from the direct-coarray facet. Facet count rose from 63 to 64.

findings.defect: Plans cited C descriptors but the dependency strings omitted the exact Clause 18 owners.
findings.correction: 18.3.7 p2/p4/p6 and 18.5.3 p1-p5 added and verified against the census.

explicit_limitations: Source registration only: no test program, compiler invocation, oracle, canonical link, SourceUse relationship or fixture approval is created.
All 64 facets remain pending. Coarray facets are gated on the separately provisioned multi-image capability, and the stopped or failed image condition is explicitly not producible by this suite.
No plan reads deallocated storage, dereferences a deallocated pointer target, or queries an undefined pointer association status; the reviewer verified this directly.

ALLOCATE and its constraints remain owned by 9.7.1.1, allocation semantics by 9.7.1.2-9.7.1.4, NULLIFY by 9.7.2, STAT= and ERRMSG= by 9.7.4 and 9.7.5, attributes by 8.5.3 and 8.5.14, coarrays by 8.5.6, finalization by 7.5.6 and status semantics by 19.5.x and 19.6.x.
